_Requested by **Sure Team** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VhYV3jhQ9s4qrrh2th12sN?thread=cmsg_01VhYV3jhQ9s4qrrh2th12sNU8XrgcUCfrQdeesjpes4wi)_

Item: obs-live-capture

## What

A capture hook in the harness plugin (`plugins/harness/scripts/capture.mjs`, handlers in `scripts/capture-rows.mjs`) on UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop and Stop. In a project that installed the harness it appends, as they happen:

- `tool.call` {tool, inputHash, inputBytes, ms, ok}, with `agent` = the subagent's `agent_id` (null for the main session)
- `agent.spawn`, `agent.finish` (tokens summed from the agent's transcript, served model, ms)
- `brief.stored` / `result.stored`, with the texts as `journal/blobs/<sha256>`, written once (`wx`)
- `wake` {reason, source, hash, bytes} (new kind), `turn.usage` (tokens since the last Stop; cost and 5h/7d windows are null with a placeholder because no hook receives them)
- `hook.run` {name, ms since process start, timedOut}

Rows never hold tool inputs, only sha256 and size. Rows are documented in `docs/journal.md`, "Capture rows".

## Decision

`plan/decisions/2026-10-30-capture-by-hooks.md`: it uses settings hooks, not a mod. Mods need the person to turn them on in each session, and hooks already carry `agent_id`, `duration_ms` and the subagent transcript paths. The files go in `scripts/` because the env-bootstrap verifier test reads hook commands as `scripts/<file>`.

## Evidence (builder)

- `plugins/harness/test/capture.test.mjs` (11 tests) replays a recorded `claude -p` session. It has 2 main calls and 1 subagent with 2 calls, and the fixture is in `plugins/harness/test/fixtures/capture/`, cleaned by its `make.mjs` so it holds no env, account or cwd fields. The replay goes through the handlers and through the hook process. It checks rows against `expected.json`, one `tool.call` per PostToolUse and none extra, blobs stored once, and hook.run median and p95.
- A live headless session with `--plugin-dir plugins/harness` journalled each row within ms of the call. A background subagent's brief wasn't yet in its transcript at SubagentStart, so `brief.stored` now comes from the Agent call's PostToolUse.
- hook.run in an idle replay: about 40 ms median. On the project-files mount it was 38 to 63 ms, with a tail to 160 ms. While a live session ran in this container it was about 55 to 66 ms.
- `npm test`: 159 pass, and the 1 failure is the clean-room "green" test that is already red on main (release version check, which another thread is fixing).

brief and final answer are stored once as blobs by sha256. Tests replay a recorded session (fixtures/capture).
Adds the wake kind. Decision: plan/decisions/2026-10-30-capture-by-hooks.md.

commit.message:
obs-live-capture: take the brief from the Agent call, so background agents get theirs

A background agent's transcript may not be written when SubagentStart runs (seen live), so brief.stored and its blob
come from the Agent tool's PostToolUse (prompt and the agentId it returns). agent.spawn keeps briefHash when the
transcript already has it, else null with a placeholder.

obs-live-capture: run capture async on tool calls and subagent stops

The verifier measured capture at a 60 ms median in live sessions, over the item's 50 ms. Run in line, every tool
call would wait for that; run async (PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure), Claude Code goes on without waiting.
SubagentStop is async and first waits for the subagent's transcript to stop growing: in a live run the hook read it
20 ms before the hand-back line landed and lost the answer. UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart and Stop stay in line,
because an async Stop was lost when a headless session exited.

+# Capture by settings hooks, not a mod
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-30, by the obs-live-capture thread, on the person's standing instruction to decide two-way doors and
+not wait.
+
+**The item asked for** "plugins/harness/hooks/capture (mod module, with a hooks fallback)".
+
+**What was seen** (a `claude -p` session on Claude Code 2.1.314 with a plugin logging every hook's input, recorded as
+`plugins/harness/test/fixtures/capture/`):
+
+- PostToolUse carries `tool_use_id`, `duration_ms` and, inside a subagent, `agent_id` and `agent_type`; the main
+  session's calls carry no `agent_id`. That is the attribution the item wants, with no guessing.
+- SubagentStart carries the new agent's id and type. The agent's transcript, whose first line is the brief, and a
+  `meta.json` naming the spawning tool use id already exist when it runs. SubagentStop carries the agent's
+  transcript path, from which its tokens, time and final answer (its SubagentHandback message) are read.
+- UserPromptSubmit carries the prompt (the wake) and Stop the transcript path (turn tokens).
+- Mods a thread writes load only after the person turns them on in each session
+  (plan/decisions/2026-10-30-setup-script-vs-sessionstart.md), and a mod's hooks see the same calls.
+
+**Choice:** capture ships as settings hooks in the harness plugin (`scripts/capture.mjs`, handlers in
+`scripts/capture-rows.mjs`), on every session the setup script builds. No mod module is built now. If a later item
+needs a mod (engine-host), it can import `capture-rows.mjs`, whose handlers take a hook-shaped input and write nothing.
+
+**Why:** the hooks carry every field the rows need and run without the person, so the "fallback" covers everything;
+a mod would add a second path that only runs where the person has switched mods on.
+
+**Async on tool calls.** The PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure capture hooks are declared `"async": true`. A probe on 2.1.314 (a PostToolUse hook doing `sleep 3`
+marked async) showed the next tool call start 1.1 s after the previous one ended, not 3 s, while the hook still
+finished and wrote. The verifier measured capture's own run at a 60 ms median in live sessions (42 ms in the idle
+fixture run), of which about 22 ms is node starting. Run in line, that would put 60 ms on every call, over the item's
+50 ms; run async, the call doesn't wait for it, and `hook.run`'s `ms` is the background run's length, not time added
+to the call. Rows still land within milliseconds of the call (the verifier saw 7 to 72 ms). SubagentStop is async too, because it waits for the subagent's transcript to settle: in a live run the hook read
+the file 20 ms before the hand-back line was written, and lost the answer and the last message's tokens.
+UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart and Stop stay in line: with all of them async, a
+headless `claude -p` session exited before its final Stop hook wrote `turn.usage`. A tool call made just before a
+headless session exits can lose its row the same way; a thread's session stays up, so this is a headless-only edge.
+
+**What it costs:** one background node process per tool call, and cost and the 5-hour and 7-day usage windows, which reach no hook. `turn.usage` carries them as
+null with a placeholder. Reversible: a mod can replace the hook entry at any time.
+
+**Where:** the entry and handlers sit in `scripts/` beside the other hooks, not in a `hooks/capture/` folder as the
+item's output line named, because the env-bootstrap verifier's test reads every hook command as `scripts/<file>`.

+## Capture
+
+`scripts/capture.mjs` (plan item obs-live-capture), timeout 5 s, its own watchdog at 3 s, on UserPromptSubmit,
+PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop and Stop. On PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure and SubagentStop
+it is `async`: Claude Code starts it and goes on without waiting, so a tool call is never held up by it (a node process
+takes about 40 ms idle and 60 ms under load, mostly its own start). On SubagentStop it first waits for the subagent's
+transcript to stop growing (150 ms quiet, 2 s at most), because Claude Code can still be writing the last lines.
+UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart and Stop run in line: they come once a turn or once an agent, and an async Stop hook
+was lost when a headless session exited straight after it. In an installed project it appends a row per
+wake, tool call, subagent start and finish and turn to `journal/sessions/<session>.jsonl`, stores each subagent's
+brief and final answer once under `journal/blobs/<sha256>`, and ends with a `hook.run` row giving its own time. It
+prints nothing. The rows are in `docs/journal.md`, "Capture rows"; the handlers are in `scripts/capture-rows.mjs`, and
+the tests replay a recorded session (`test/fixtures/capture/`, remade by its `make.mjs`) through them. The Stop
+handler keeps how far it read the transcript under `$CCP_HARNESS_STATE`, never under the plugin root.
+
+It is a settings hook, not a mod: mods load only after the person turns them on for each session, and hooks carry
+every field the rows need (plan/decisions/2026-10-30-capture-by-hooks.md).
+
